title: Has anyone actually gotten good results with Tripo?
author: fukinuhhh
selftext:
Every video demoing Tripo is sponsored, and/or they are just trying to push affiliate links, this makes me skeptical. 

Has anyone had any good game ready results with Tripo? I used the free demo and it was not that great. Body was ok, the face was blurry and weird. Although, the tools locked behind paywalls intrigue me. Such as smart mesh, retries, uploading multiple images, etc.

comments.author: Ok-Leading8654
comments.body: 3D props, absolutely worth a shot. For 3D models used as armor or characters that are going to do animations.. Mind you I've only used Meshy for actual npc/player models, with fairly simple animations working great, but any movement requiring a lot of shoulder movement needing substantial repairs. Maybe Tripo models perform better with no collapsing or pinching shoulders? I'm not sure, you can get a month of trial for $8 or so, might be worth trying it out?

comments.author: Sencha-Games
comments.body:
The toplogy I get for characters is acceptable for higher levels of graphical fidelity. For lower poly games (which I tend to want to make), it prioritizes subtle details over keeping silhouettes.

Its UV maps and textures are disgusting. And I used the paid version.

Luckily, modeling low poly characters isn't the hard part. So I can do that myself and ask Claude to handle UV unwrapping and even rigging, while I make the textures and animations.

comments.author: Specialist_Top_6079
comments.body: Yep i got a kayak, a skiff, outboard motors, and water ramps done nice.  Haven't worked with characters yet except an animation I made quickly that works, but it needs a lot of cleanup on that one.

comments.author: jungle_jimjim
comments.body: The smart mesh option is great, but the textures vary. If you want to have a face that looks good from up close I’d project the face onto the model using blender or not use AI at all.

comments.author: PositiveScarcity8909
comments.body: I used it to good results but I don't need high detail models.

comments.author: DancinFool82
comments.body: I use Meshy and get amazing results! I'd assume tripo gives similar results. Maybe it's the source you're feeding in? Have you tried some different variations?

comments.author: benjaminabel
comments.body: Simple models - no issues at all. Complex characters - the reference for Smart Mesh has to be impeccable and it still needs additional fixes in Blender if you want it perfect.

comments.author: re-skob
comments.body: Yeah, Tripo has been awesome on all my projects. I did all of the buildings in my driving game with Tripo and recently used it for the Epic MegaJam with good results for human characters

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
yes but you have to pay basically. Their free tier is 2-3 years ago and it is pretty bad by today's standards

their paid model can produce quad models and there are texturing/rigging options.

I am not a 3d artist so I don't know how well they actually measure up to the standards.

I used a mix of premade assets and tripo assets in this game and it works okay: [https://chooon.itch.io/superhero-mayhem-simulator](https://chooon.itch.io/superhero-mayhem-simulator)

comments.author: MrMortlocke
comments.body:
Honestly, it helps me get started. And I often do touch-ups myself afterwards though to get the finer details and textures and stuff. 

Overall, it does a great job getting the main shape and look down.

comments.author: Sacred_B
comments.body: I'm doing low fidelity stuff and it's working fine for me.

comments.author: PoopsMcScoots
comments.body: I have been struggling, but that may be on me.
